ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The central intersection point in the figure represents a central carbon atom; it is connected to three Br to the left, upward, and downward respectively, and to a PPh3 group to the right. A positive charge is marked near P, and there is also an independent Br with a negative charge in the upper right. There are curved arrows in the figure, but the problem asks to ignore these arrows. Reasoning: After ignoring the arrows, the structure can be transcribed as tribromomethyl connected to positively charged triphenylphosphine, namely BrC(Br)(Br)[P+](Ph)3; the three phenyl groups are each written as c1ccccc1. The independent bromide ion is connected as a disconnected component with a dot, written as [Br-].

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First, ignore the arrows as instructed. Transcribe the connectivity in the image: the central carbon has three bromine substituents and one bond to positively charged triphenylphosphorus. Convert the three phenyl rings of PPh3 into three c1ccccc1 substituents on [P+]. Then add the separate bromide anion as a disconnected component after a dot. The resulting SMILES is BrC(Br)(Br)[P+](c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1.[Br-].
